subject: Commit blend schedule & term discount — proposal and milestones
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@nebula.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonah Price <j.price@nebula.ai>
Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 13:03:00 -0800
Subject: Structuring a multi-year prepay — blended commit question

Hi Rachel,

Following up from our runbook review last week — thanks again for the walkthrough. We are looking to lock in Dedicated capacity for a production feature that will ramp through 2027 and 2028. Our procurement team prefers a multi-year prepay, but they want an annualized schedule that matches our expected product growth rather than a single front-loaded prepay.

High level:
- Year 1: conservative launch (small fleet + cache-heavy usage)
- Year 2: customer expansion, expect ~2.5x tokens and 3x sustained concurrent sessions
- Year 3: peak steady state

Questions:
1) Can you propose a blended commit (GPU / sustained TPM) schedule we could sign to today that escalates capacity over three years?
2) How do term discounts change if we annualize the prepay vs a single up-front prepay?
3) What happens operationally if we exceed the committed TPM in year 1 — do we get automatic throttles, overage billing, or temporary burst credits?

Procurement will want numbers to run through legal and finance. Can you and the team put a concrete proposal together? We can share expected token/day profiles if that helps.

Thanks,
Elena
Head of Platform
Nebula AI

---
Attachment: runbook_prod_feature_v1.pdf (referenced)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@nebula.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Jonah Price <j.price@nebula.ai>, procurement@nebula.ai
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Structuring a multi-year prepay — blended commit question

Elena —

Appreciate the detail, this is exactly the right framing. I attached a first-pass proposal (Redwood_Dedicated_Commit_Tiers_v2.pdf) and a simple milestone workbook (Proposed_Milestones.xlsx) that maps commits to target TPM/GPU and the suggested term discounts. High-level summary below, then some asks so we can finalize numbers for procurement: 

Proposal (summary):
- 3‑year blended commit, signed up-front but annualized in our invoice schedule (we can offer annual invoices tied to year milestones).
- Year 1: 8 reserved GPUs + 500k TPM baseline (conservative launch); Year 2: 20 GPUs + 1.25M TPM; Year 3: 32 GPUs + 2.0M TPM.
- Term discount: 10% on list for annualized 3‑year blend, 14% if Nebula elects full up‑front prepay for all three years.
- Overages: token overages billed monthly at the discounted overage rate; short bursts handled with an agreed burst allowance (up to 20% over baseline for up to 72 hours) before overage rates apply.

Asks / next inputs we need from you: 
- Confirmation on whether you want invoices annualized (we can annualize payment but the contract is single-term).
- Expected token/day distribution for first 6 months to check cold cache hit ratios and recommend prefix cache sizing.
- Any procurement constraints around PO vs contract signature cadence.

I'll loop in Karthik to validate the proposed GPU/TPM mapping (he's got the detailed perf curves). Also copying Vivek for finance/discount approval lanes. If that looks directionally right, I'll prepare a marked-up SOW and a short mutual action plan.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive — Dedicated
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_Commit_Tiers_v2.pdf; Proposed_Milestones.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Elena Morales <elena@nebula.ai>, Jonah Price <j.price@nebula.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 11:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Structuring a multi-year prepay — blended commit question

Rachel / Elena —

Quick technical notes to align the TPM<>GPU mapping in the deck:
- Baseline assumptions: production mix is 60% short chat-like requests (avg len 80 tokens) and 40% batch generative (avg len 600 tokens). Cache hit expected to be ~30% first 3 months and improve to 50% with prompt templating and prefix caching.
- The proposed 8 GPUs at 500k TPM baseline assumes 1.5x continuous utilization during daytime peak with aggressive batching; it is conservative for cold-cache conditions.
- Ramp cadence suggestion (milestones):
  * M1 (launch, month 0–3): 8 GPUs, 500k TPM baseline, 20% burst allowance
  * M2 (scale, month 4–12): add 6 GPUs at month 4, target 14 GPUs and 750k TPM baseline by month 7
  * M3 (expansion, year 2 start): stock to 20 GPUs and 1.25M TPM baseline through automated scale operations
  * M4 (steady state, year 3): 32 GPUs and 2.0M TPM baseline with adjusted KV cache pools and optimized kernels
- Operational behaviour on exceed: overages are charged at negotiated rate; we can also configure a soft-fail policy that routes noncritical traffic to a lower‑cost model variant before billing overage.

If procurement wants a list of gating metrics for the annualized invoice triggers (e.g., MRR attainment, API error rate < 0.5%), we can propose objective milestones in the SOW. Happy to join a call next week to walk through the workbook.

—Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: procurement@nebula.ai <procurement@nebula.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Elena Morales <elena@nebula.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 08:11:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Structuring a multi-year prepay — blended commit question

Rachel / team —

Two quick procurement clarifications from our side after reviewing the PDF: 
1) The finance team prefers annual invoices rather than an up-front full prepay — they asked whether the 10% discount for annualized billing is fixed or can be improved if we commit to a minimum annual PO cadence.
2) For the burst allowance, can you confirm whether those bursts consume reserved GPUs first or are routed to burst pool capacity that would incur separate charges?

We can schedule a 30-minute econ call if helpful.

Thanks,
Procurement Team
Nebula AI

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: procurement@nebula.ai, Elena Morales <elena@nebula.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Structuring a multi-year prepay — blended commit question

Procurement / Elena —

Thanks — quick clarifications and next steps below.

Answers:
- Discounting: the 10% we floated is our standard blended term discount for annualized billing on the 3‑year commit. We can improve to 12% if Nebula commits to an annual PO cadence (each year invoiced upfront at the agreed annual milestone) and signs within 2 weeks. If procurement is comfortable with a single full up‑front payment, we can offer 14% as previously noted. Vivek, finance has greenlight to approve up to 12% for the PO cadence path.
- Burst allowance mechanics: bursts consume available reserved capacity first; once reserved capacity is saturated, traffic enters the burst pool and is billed at the agreed overage rate. We will configure a soft-fail routing policy to fall back to a compatible cheaper model variant before overage billing kicks in (we'll list the variant in the SOW).

Proposed next steps:
1) Rachel to send a redlineable SOW + mutual action plan (I'll attach markups in the DocuSign packet).
2) Procurement to confirm preferred invoicing cadence (annual PO vs full up-front).
3) Schedule an econ call this week to lock discount % and milestone acceptance criteria (I am available Wed/Thu 9–12 PT).

I'll prepare the SOW that reflects the M1–M4 milestones in the workbook and the three discount paths (annualized 10%, annual PO cadence 12%, full prepay 14%). Once we align, I'll drop a DocuSign link and a draft PO template for procurement to review.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive — Dedicated
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_Commit_Tiers_v2.pdf; Proposed_Milestones.xlsx
